explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation by comparing GPT-4 and human pairwise preference evaluations on the same Dolly test prompts, reporting agreement rates and conducting re-annotation studies to measure human-human and human-LLM agreement

prompts.notes: Full prompt template provided in Appendix H.3, including system preamble and detailed evaluation criteria

guidelines.notes: Detailed human evaluation guidelines provided in Appendix H.4, including specific ranking criteria and instructions for handling ties and incomprehensible prompts

sample_size.notes: Validation conducted on subsets of 100 Dolly test prompts per language model comparison pair, with re-annotation studies

validation_results.summary_finding: Human-GPT-4 agreement rates vary by language (61-83%), with overall moderate agreement (avg κ=0.38) suggesting LLM evaluation captures human preferences reasonably well but with notable differences in specific cases

criteria_mapping.notes: GPT-4 evaluates based on factuality and semantic comprehensibility criteria, while human evaluators also consider creativity and personal preference when other criteria are fulfilled
